mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation surprises are strongly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent recovery in residential construction, resulting in a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as sector rotation boosts construction-related equities.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes or construction sector underperforms the index by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures, pushing firms' cost structures higher and compressing profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or inflation-adjusted corporate margins expand during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns as earnings expectations deteriorate across cyclicals, over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes or the industrial sector outperforms the index by more than 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which typically reduces risk appetite and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or inflation expectations fall during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs in a single month, without a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate, signals a hidden slack in the labor market that precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -100000 AND UNRATE monthly change >= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes or payroll employment recovers within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) for four consecutive months, accompanied by stable unemployment, signals weakening consumer demand outside of labor-market weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discretionary sector earnings expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < 0% for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE monthly change >= -0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes or retail sector outperforms the index by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between the year-over-year change in GDP (GDPC1) and S&P 500 20-day returns implies that macroeconomic expansion is a persistent driver of equity gains; the mechanism predicts positive returns when GDPC1 YoY growth is above its 5-year average.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above median in periods when GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds its 5-year average (t-test p > 0.10).
